“Countless billions of garments, pure, excellent, and subtle,
swiftly transform and deliver their elders and superiors, causing them never again to harbor doubt. Furthermore,
there was a bodhisattva named Dhyānāhāra, who spoke a verse before the Buddha:
"Those who have faith in this profound sutra should be provided with excellent food,
complete with all flavors, as they single-mindedly practice the conduct of the Great Sage.
Furthermore, there was a bodhisattva named Jñānadarśana-āryasthita who spoke a verse before the Buddha, saying:
“Those who harbor doubts regarding this sutra shall give rise to sorrow;
weeping and shedding tears, they will not believe in the profound Dharma of the sutra.
Whether coming from the hells or returning to the evil realms,”
In the space of a mere moment, they harbor doubts regarding this image-dharma;
seized by evil companions, they do not understand the profound and subtle meaning;
bound by the net of doubt, they therefore resort to what is not the right place.
Thus failing to accord with right precepts, observing anger and harboring resentment while dwelling in such a state, they are likened to ferocious beasts.
Neither cultivating the path nor practicing skillful means, they are indolent and lack diligence.
Believing in the heterodox and lacking wisdom, they do not believe in these scriptures.
They long for the beginning and end of all living beings, clinging to the self and to affection;
dependent on the afflictions of the triple world, they do not believe in this subtle and wondrous [Dharma].
Harboring malice is the mark of ignorance and darkness;
Attached to the pleasures of desire, they greedily cling to their own bodies, And thus slander this teaching of the Way.
Their minds long for fine clothing, And they pursue delicious food and drink.
Because they retain but little of the pure and white Dharma, they slander this sutra.
Dwelling in the realm of desire and pleasure, they crave what lacks virtue and reality;
such persons distance themselves from it and do not draw near to the World-Honored One.
Furthermore, there was a bodhisattva named Abandoning Evil Dharmas, who spoke a verse before the Buddha:
"One should abandon such people, just as one stays far from a latrine;
the fool doubts this sutra, yet clings to the realms while seeking liberation."
One should avoid it together [with others], just as one avoids a corpse reeking of death;
those who doubt this profound sutra should distance themselves from it in such a manner.
Those who slander it are like bandits threatening a village.
Thus dwelling in a dark place, one sees evil intentions flee.
Upon observing this, one should immediately hasten away; these are thieves, fierce and evil things.
If one slanders this sutra, one will not see the mind’s lack of confusion.
At that time, Ānanda came forward and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"Never before has there been such a thing,
O God among Gods!"
Is it that these bodhisattvas possess such analytical wisdom regarding the sutras?
Is it through the power of samādhi that they speak these words?
Or do they understand them by receiving the Buddha’s holy intent?
The Buddha said:
"By relying on the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power and through the meaning of this sutra, one attains the power of samādhi and reaches the unconditioned (asaṃskṛta). Why is this so?..."
Now these sons of noble family who abide here have heard this scripture from sixty billion buddhas, and they have believed, delighted in, praised, and recited it;
likewise, through their resolve in the power of samādhi and sustained by the majestic spiritual authority of the Buddha, they now expound this scripture.
"Why is this? As it has been stated, they are equal and without distinction; this constitutes clear evidence.
Ānanda asked the Buddha:
“If a son of noble family or a daughter of noble family hears this sutra and immediately rejoices with faith, free from doubt, what merit and blessings will they obtain?
The Buddha told Ānanda:

“If a son of noble family or a daughter of noble family aspires to the unsurpassed, right, and true path, and were to fill this entire world with the seven treasures to offer as a gift to the Tathāgata;”
"If there were another person who, upon hearing this profound sutra, immediately rejoices with faith and does not harbor doubt, their merit would surpass that of the former.
The Buddha said,
"Let us set aside these treasures filling the entire world."
If one were to fill as many Buddha-worlds as there are grains of sand in the Ganges with precious jewels to make offerings to the Tathāgatas,
the merit of one who hears this sutra and rejoices with faith would surpass that.
At that time, the Buddha spoke in verse:
"Even if this entire world were filled with the seven treasures,
and one were to offer them all as a gift to the Tathāgata, the World-Honored One who has realized the wisdom of truth."
When wise people hear this sutra, they believe and rejoice without wavering;
this merit is supreme, and its virtue is beyond limit.
Even if there were as many Buddha-fields as there are grains of sand in the Ganges, [and one were to fill them all with offerings]...
“Making offerings to the Holy World-Honored One does not equal hearing this sutra.
Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
“If sons or daughters of good family hear this Dharma of the sutra and, with joy and faith, uphold, recite, and chant it, what will their merit be like?”
The Buddha said:

"If sons or daughters of good family seek unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment and for a hundred kalpas make offerings to the Tathāgata—practicing generosity, observing the precepts, practicing patience, exerting diligence, maintaining single-minded concentration, and cultivating wisdom—and furthermore attain the five supernormal powers, clearly understanding the world for each of those hundred kalpas without further doubt;
yet if they do not accept this sutra, such persons have failed to make offerings to the Buddha."
At that time, the Buddha spoke in verse:
“If one were to fulfill a hundred kalpas By offering and making worship to the World-Honored One,
Providing all manner of food and drink in abundance, Yet does not thereby truly worship the Buddha.”
Those who receive this sutra thereby honor the Great Sage;
abandoning attachment to the notion of a path, they provide the Dharma-offering to all Buddhas.
Thus following the Honored One’s teaching, they truly serve the Buddha.
The Dharma-offering is perfect awakening; the Tathāgata is the Dharma-body.
Even if one were to fill a hundred kalpas with the finest garments and offer them to the World-Honored One, the Perfectly Awakened One, this would not be an offering to the Buddha.
Those who receive this sutra shall be most honored, reverent, and solemn;
they should be served as if they were the Buddha himself, far surpassing those who offer robes and garments.
Even if, throughout a hundred kalpas, one were to offer bright pearls, exquisite flowers, and fragrances, [it would not equal the merit of receiving this sutra].
To approach the World-Honored One, the Fully Awakened One, and not offer worship to the Buddha;
yet if there are those who receive this sutra and eliminate all notions of reliance and fruit—
this is indeed worshiping the World-Honored One’s supreme wisdom.
If one were to erect stupas made of the seven treasures for the sake of the Hero of the World,
all as high as Mount Sumeru, yet not for the purpose of making offerings to the Buddha;
whereas if one were to receive this sutra and not perceive a self, [the latter would be far superior].
This is the most honored offering, supreme among all things.
Even if one were to observe the prohibitions and precepts for a full hundred kalpas,
yet fail to uphold this scripture, those precepts would lack renown.
Those who receive this sutra possess the great renown of these precepts;
if one upholds the pure precepts, there are no precepts superior to these.
Immeasurable and inconceivable, the wise and brilliant follow this sutra.
Serving through causes and conditions, one’s prohibitions are always fully maintained.
When those prohibitions are entirely perfected, it cannot be said that the precepts have been violated;
one who studies this sutra should act exactly according to these instructions.
Those who do not study this sutra are not seeking the Buddha-way;
though they may fully uphold the sages, they have nothing to learn.
Practicing the precepts in such a manner, one should discern the meaning of this sutra.
Those who uphold this scroll will be fully endowed with the prohibitive precepts.
Even if, throughout a hundred kalpas, they single-mindedly practice patience,
should there be those who revile them with anger, they shall endure all such people.
If one receives this sutra, hearing, upholding, and reciting it with patience, this is the most supreme; it is subtle and immeasurable.
Even if one’s hands or feet are severed, the mind never harbors resentment.
Neither weary nor distressed, their minds never stir from the beginning.
Such patience as this, practiced for a hundred kalpas—
those who follow it in this way possess no grasping toward this patience.
If one receives this sutra, hearing, retaining, and reciting it,
this patience is the most supreme, subtle and immeasurable.
If one holds this scroll of the sutra, that patience is the most supreme.
Sublime and peerless, he is free from all falsehood;
He never ceases his teaching of utmost sincerity. The Buddha’s wisdom is unsurpassed;
One who does not disparage this sutra Shall attain all their wishes as they desire.
Even if one were to practice with diligence and without indolence for a hundred eons,
rising early and sleeping late without ceasing, one might achieve all one's wishes;
yet if one studies this sutra and expounds it, one will attain clear wisdom.
This diligence is supreme; in its ardent cultivation, none can surpass it.
Even if one were to become a seer with the five supernatural powers for a full hundred kalpas, if they do not hear this sutra, they possess no true spiritual power.
If one receives this Dharma, discerning it without attachment, one attains mastery of the supernormal powers; there is nothing superior to this.
Even if one were to cultivate and honor wisdom for a hundred eons, [it would not equal this].
Transcending the world with clear illumination, they delight in the conduct upon which they rely;
if one does not study this fascicle, wisdom will not be perfected.
This holy one, who has attained penetration and is courageous, is able to uphold this profound sutra.
This is the knowledge of the Path, the clear comprehension of noble wisdom;
if one hears the essentials of the profound sutras, one receives and upholds them with joy.
Possessing discerning, deep wisdom, one understands the destination of all phenomena.
One should follow what is spoken in this sutra; such is the wisdom of this image.
Cultivating the true scriptures, one’s single wisdom is non-dual;
therefore, cultivate the practice of vigor and faithfully uphold these essential texts.
At that time, the Venerable Ānanda spoke in verse before the Buddha:
"Even if it be four thousand li away, or even further than four thousand li,
one would go to hear this sutra, in order to follow and attain the fruits of the Buddha's virtues."
He then went directly to that person's house, not regarding the way as difficult;
the wise should travel swiftly, propagating this sutra wherever they go.
Those who wish to quickly engage in meditative contemplation and transcend all things [should do so].
Reciting and expounding the path of this sutra, upholding it and understanding its meaning;
if one seeks all forms of peace, aspires to the bodhisattva practice,
and lectures upon this scripture, one shall reach the Land of Peace and Bliss.
"One shall behold the Equal Enlightenment, Amitābha’s state of non-thought;
thus one cultivates in accordance with the meaning of the sūtra, as expounded by all Buddhas.
The Buddha said:
“Excellent, excellent, Ānanda!
It is exactly as you have said; it is precisely so, without any difference.”
When sons or daughters of good family praise this sutra and recite it, their minds will not be distracted and they will be free from all conceptualizations;
while remaining in their own homes, they shall behold the Buddha, the World-Honored One.
If one praises this sutra without distraction, at the time of death, one will behold countless Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, with one's own eyes. Why is this?
It is because all Buddhas protect and sustain such sons and daughters of good family; it is brought about by their upholding, reading, reciting, and chanting this sutra.

Chapter Fifteen: The Chapter on the Daughter of the Teacher. From the *Anavatapta-nirdeśa-sūtra*, Chapter Fifteen: The Chapter on the Daughter of the Teacher. At that time, the maiden Śrīmatī, together with five hundred maidens, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“Indeed, World-Honored One!”
"If women were to study this sutra, what merit would they obtain?
And if they were to recite, chant, and read it, where would their blessings lead?
The Buddha said:
“If a woman seeks the unsurpassed, true, and correct path and wishes to study this sutra, she should observe other women.

Why is this? If one studies this sutra with single-minded devotion and without distraction, yet does not emulate other women who crave worldly toil, it is precisely because of such causes that one receives a female body.”
Ishu asked again: "What is meant by the afflictions of women?
Being deluded by desire, why do they receive a female body?"
He replied: "If there is a woman who, seeing another woman who is upright, beautiful, and adorned with precious necklaces, does not feel longing for her, but instead observes herself."
For example, it is like a foul latrine that the mind finds unpleasant; one contemplates it as a defiled road and does not regard it as clean.
If one craves and delights in such things, one will receive a female body.
Furthermore, it is reckoned that women are often full of jealousy; their hearts and mouths differ from one another, failing to correspond, and their words do not accord with their actions.
Even when they see a bhikṣu, they seek only fame and reputation, having no regard for the sūtras or the Dharma, and they harbor much anger.
One who delights in socializing with guests and has never sought such a sūtra as this for the sake of profit—
if such a person reads or recites it, their mind will be attached to seeking gain, their resolve will be confused and distracted, and they will wander amidst the dust of worldly defilements.
For this reason, one who has received a female form cannot eliminate their offenses.
However, if a woman were to eliminate her craving and desire, refrain from giving rise to perverse thoughts, receive the root text of this sutra, and uphold, recite, and read it.
"Why is this? Because this profound and honored sutra removes the dust and color of womanhood.
He asked again:
"If a woman does not desire her own body, but receives this sutra-dharma, upholds it, recites it, and reads it,
by what causes and conditions will she transform from a female form?
The Buddha said:
"If you wish to transform your female body, receive these scriptures, uphold, recite, and read them; do not desire womanhood, for it is always feared as something defiled.
It is like a person who, seeing a great blazing fire, throws himself into its midst while saying with his own mouth:
'Do not let the fire burn me; do not let it wound my skin.'"
“What do you think, young woman?
If that person were to say ‘yes,’ would he obtain his wish? She replied:
"It is not so, O God among Gods! Why is this? Because..."
"Considering that the Lord of the Fire-seed burns whatever it encounters, causing the flesh and sinews to rot and decay,
it cannot be without injury. The Buddha said, "It is so."
This sutra is likewise; it burns away the dust of worldly desire until nothing remains.
Should one become attached to the states of sensual passion, one will endanger oneself for many lifetimes.

Therefore, if a woman wishes to transform this body, quickly attain the ultimate realization of the Noble Path, behold countless Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, and be endowed with immeasurable eloquence, she should receive this sutra, uphold it, recite it, and read it.
The maiden Priyangu and her five hundred companions addressed the Buddha, saying:
“We have reflected upon this,
World-Honored One!”

In the past, from the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Dīpaṃkara, he received this sūtra text, upheld, recited, and read it, and expounded its meaning for immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of beings.
Ānanda said to the Buddha:
“This Śikhaṇḍin, though her body is that of a woman, is not actually a woman. Why is this so?”
Now, as I observe with my own eyes for the last time, I am personally amazed that a young girl could manifest such transformations.
Out of compassion for women, he sought to deliver them; by withdrawing all the men so they could not be seen, he moved them to convert the multitude of women.
The Buddha said, “Ānanda!
As for that *pārṣukā*, it is neither male nor female; such a thing does not exist.”
Why is this? When one contemplates the fundamental nature of all phenomena (*dharmas*), one finds neither man nor woman; all phenomena are unobtainable, being equal and without distinction.
Why is this so? Calculated in this way, she is neither male nor female.
The maiden Priyadarśanā, having analyzed this sutra, was free from all obstructions and attained the light of the Dharma.
Therefore, Ānanda! If there are women who desire to become men, they should follow this method of private restorative practice and receive, uphold, recite, and read this sutra scroll.
At that time, five hundred bhikṣuṇīs came forward and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"We, of our kind, from this day forward shall receive the original text of this sutra, uphold it, recite it, and read it."
He took no pleasure in women and felt loathing and revulsion for this body.
From this day forward, he would no longer sit or sleep; he recited this sutra until he had mastered it and attained concentration.
Then the Buddha praised her, saying: "Excellent!
To recite these words as you have spoken them is to don the great armor of virtue, to achieve mastery through diligence, and to have no longing for the form of a woman."
"Therefore, O virtuous ones!
You should apply yourselves even more diligently to practice, receive this sūtra text, and uphold, recite, and read it.
When the bhikṣuṇīs heard what the Buddha had said, they were filled with great joy; they immediately removed their robes and draped them over the Buddha, and uttered this eulogy:
"I have attained happiness today; I hope to obtain a male body.
The words of the Perfectly Awakened One do not differ from reality; I shall certainly attain the state of World-Honored One.
Thereupon, the wives of the five hundred elders, hearing that the bhikṣuṇīs had donned these armor-like virtues, immediately rose from their seats, approached the Buddha, and addressed him.
"O God among Gods! From this day forward, we shall receive, uphold, recite, and read this sutra scroll.
We pray that we may attain mastery, not be bound by others, not have to observe the countenances of others, and be free from the afflictions of the Māra-sent ones and their stubborn obstacles."
Why is this so? Even if a woman is born into a royal family, she is subject to another and lacks independence; for the duration of her life, she must serve her husband.
Therefore, from this day forward, we shall at last observe diligent effort.

Even if someone were to expound a single phrase of the meaning within this sutra, we would not dare to slander it; until the end of our lives, we shall not approach our husbands, so that you may cause us to read and understand this sutra.
Then the World-Honored One praised the wife of the elder, saying:
“Excellent, excellent!
These women have now uttered a great lion’s roar before the Buddha; these words are most admirable, for they have donned the armor of the infinite.”
Just as one whose aspirations do not examine the countenances of others, who does not bear heavy burdens, and who does not enter the womb by way of conception,
but rather gives birth in a pure Buddha-land where there are no women and no physical defects.
Ānanda asked the Buddha,
"What is the name of the world where these sisters will be reborn, such that it is free from all defects?
The Buddha said:
"The world shall be named Jewel Lotus Treasury, and you shall be born in that land.
He then asked the Buddha:
"What will be the holy name of that Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha?"
The Buddha said:
"There is a Buddha named Sarvaratnābhāsottama Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who currently dwells and teaches the Dharma."
When the wife of that elder had studied this scripture and beheld that Tathāgata, she was filled with joy and leaped for gladness as wholesome thoughts arose within her.
She immediately untied from her neck a necklace of hundreds of thousands of jewels and strings of the seven precious gems, scattering them over the Buddha, and with one voice spoke these verses:
"Today we have attained our great aspiration; We shall cast off this female body."
The Fully Awakened One’s words are without distinction; his mouth utters speech of ultimate sincerity.
You should cast off this ignorant form, the female body of calamity and sin.
Foolish and deluded, your mind is greedily attached; you do not understand that the fundamental nature is non-existent.
"No longer within a womb, having cast off the body she received,
she has attained the unsurpassed truth and has never again dwelt [in such a state].
When the householder’s wife had spoken these verses, she gazed up at the Honored One’s countenance, her eyes never blinking.

Chapter 16: Praising the Dharma Master. From the *Anavatapta-nirdeśa-sūtra*, Chapter Sixteen: Praising the Dharma Master. At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, took celestial flowers and scattered them over the Buddha, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“Indeed, World-Honored One!”
"I have received and upheld this subtle and wondrous sutra.
He replied: "Therefore, Kauśika!"
"By virtue of the grace of this sutra, the devas and asuras shall not incite warfare.

Thereupon, Mañjuśrī, wishing to transform and enlighten the multitude of countless hundreds of thousands of people so that they might establish the roots of merit, came forward and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"The Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha originally resolved upon the mind of enlightenment and recited this root of the Great Dharma."
The Buddha said:
"Therefore, O virtuous one!

Among the incalculable hundreds of billions of nayutas of bodhisattvas, the most honored one is the Sage of Radiant Wisdom, whose light pervades the lands of all Buddhas throughout the ten directions, just as the solar palace shines everywhere without exception."
When these words were spoken, this land shook in six ways, and celestial flowers rained down everywhere.
Ānanda addressed the Buddha:
“For what reason does the earth shake, and why do celestial flowers rain down?”
The Buddha told Ānanda:
“Countless billions of devas, hearing the praises and hymns of Mañjuśrī, were filled with exultation; they scattered these celestial flowers and made this vow:
‘We, too, shall receive this sūtra scroll and attain the wisdom of the Path just as Mañjuśrī has.’”
As soon as these words were spoken, all his transgressions were completely extinguished, and he was enabled to draw near to this sutra.
For this reason, he joyfully prostrated at the Buddha’s feet and again paid homage to Mañjuśrī; it is for this reason that the earth shook.
Ānanda asked the Buddha:
"The virtue of this sutra is vast and infinite.
Those who hear this sutra will attain no small measure; it is not to be encountered lightly."
The Buddha said: "It is so, Ānanda!
Only after sons and daughters of good family have made offerings to countless Buddhas in the past and present do they finally come to hear this sutra-dharma."
"If one hears and believes with joy, receives, upholds, recites, and chants it, then one shall be a holy deity above and below heaven.
The Buddha said to Ānanda:
"Wherever this sutra is circulated, it will not be in vain; there, a Buddha is present as its peer."

If there are those who receive, uphold, recite, and study it, they shall tear asunder the net and subdue the evil Māra; they shall attain the brilliance of the Dharma and manifest the light of the Dharma, exhorting and encouraging the masses in darkness so that they may reach the site of enlightenment.
If there are those who hear this scripture from me, receive and uphold it with joy, and recite and study it, they shall become children of the Buddha born from the Dharma-body.

Desiring to partake of the food of the sages and sit beneath the Bodhi tree—just as I sit when I do—and desiring to preach and expound the Dharma just as the Buddha has taught it, they should receive this scripture, uphold it, recite it, and read it.
Ānanda asked the Buddha:
"I only pray that the World-Honored One will speak of those who will come in the future; will there be anyone hereafter who receives this sutra and its Dharma, upholding, reciting, and reading it?"
The Buddha said,
"Ānanda! Those who now have faith before me, it is only in future lives that they will truly believe, uphold, and recite [this teaching]."

The Buddha observed that among those in the heavens above, the world below, and the human realm—including all Māras, Brahmās, śramaṇas, brahmins, devas, humans, and asuras—none had ever heard this sutra.
There has never been anyone in future generations who, upon hearing this, would believe and rejoice in it.
Those who hear it now will only come to believe it later.
It is like an elder or an elder’s son, possessing immeasurable wealth, who dwells alone guarding his treasures before traveling to another land.
"What do you think, Ānanda? Would that person be able to recover the treasure he had hidden? He replied:
"I have obtained it.
Why is this? Because I know its place of concealment; whenever I seek it, I obtain it immediately."
The Buddha said: "It is so.
Hearing this sutra now and taking refuge in it in future generations is like obtaining hidden treasure; the Buddha beholds it here with the eye of the Way."
Those who, in this present life, hear this Dharma of the sutra and with joy and faith accept, uphold, recite, and chant it,
will certainly obtain the same in future lives as well, Ānanda!
"Sit before the Buddha and listen to this profound sutra.
Chapter 17: On Slandering At that time, Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
"If there are those who hear this sutra but do not believe or rejoice in it, instead reviling, disparaging, and slandering it—where will their transgressions lead?"
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"Be silent for now; what is the use of this question?
Ānanda addressed the Buddha:
“I pray that the Buddha will explain this.
If there are those who do not believe, they may perhaps reform themselves upon hearing of the sin of slandering [the Dharma].
The Buddha said:
“If one were to commit the five heinous crimes, and furthermore were to take the lives of all beings in a trichiliocosm, what would their transgression be like?
Ānanda replied, “It would be exceedingly great, exceedingly great.”
"O God among Gods!
The calamities will be immeasurable.
The Buddha said:
“The offense of one who slanders the Dharma reaches this magnitude.

Suppose there were another person who destroyed and damaged as many stūpas and monasteries of the Buddhas as there are grains of sand along the banks of the Ganges, and after the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, burned down those monasteries with fire—would their offense not be even greater?”
He replied: "Very many, very many,
O God among Gods!"
"Such people as these should not see or hear [this].
The Buddha said, "Ānanda!"
I shall now explain this transgression for that person.
Furthermore, if there were someone who destroys, disrupts, and extinguishes the Buddha-dharma of the past, future, and present, what would their transgression be like?
Ānanda said, "That offense is exceedingly deep; it cannot be measured or calculated.
The Buddha said:
“The calamity for one who slanders this sutra is as such. [The interlocutor asked:
“If one prevents others from studying it, what shall be their transgression?
The Buddha said:
"Suppose all sentient beings in the trichiliocosm were to practice the ten virtuous paths and further resolve their minds upon the unsurpassed, perfect, and true path.
If there were a single person who gouged out the eyes of them all, how would the gravity of that person's sin compare?"
Ānanda said: "The transgression is exceedingly great,
O World-Honored One!"
"For incalculable kalpas, you shall constantly be born blind, and furthermore, the suffering of being burned by the fires of the hells will never end.
The Buddha said to Ānanda,
"I therefore speak to you with earnestness and entrust this to you."
"Suppose there were someone who slanders and prohibits another person from practicing this Dharma; their sin would exceed that [of the former].
Ānanda asked again:
"If, furthermore, there were someone who aspires to seek the Great Way and, though harboring doubts regarding this sutra, does not slander it, where would their karma lead?"
The Buddha said:
"If a person harbors doubts for as many moments as they have entertained them throughout their past lives, they shall always remain distant from the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones.
According to the number of those doubts, they shall further be separated from the Way and its Teachings for as many kalpas as there were such doubts."
Ānanda said to the Buddha:

"If one does not believe with joy, but instead restrains others and prevents them from learning it, how great will that person's suffering be in their future body, and how many punishments will they receive?"
The Buddha said,
“Stop, Ānanda! What is the use of this question?”
Ānanda addressed the Buddha:
“I pray that the World-Honored One will expound this.

Among these four assemblies, there may be some who are like this; furthermore, in future ages, when the people of great nations in the borderlands hear this Dharma of the sutra, many will harbor doubts. May you cause them to believe and understand, so that they no longer slander it.”
The Buddha said,
"That person’s body shall be ten thousand *ya* tall, and they will experience pervasive, diligent suffering and poisonous pain beyond measure.
Ānanda asked the Buddha:
“How large is his tongue?
The Buddha said:

“His tongue is forty thousand *li* in both width and length. For five hundred billion years he shall drive a plow to till his own tongue; for another five hundred billion years he shall swallow molten copper, its flames blazing fiercely, while rain falls upon his body, burning, scorching, and boiling him.”
"Why is this? It is because of this failure to guard the tongue.

Thereupon, the hair on the bodies of the fourfold assembly who had gathered there stood on end; they wept in fear, fell prostrate upon the ground, and simultaneously raised their voices to seek mercy and repent for their transgressions:

"You should pray for these good men and good women to be delivered from their offenses; they shall then suffer various agonizing pains, their bodies becoming so vast that the suffering is beyond description."
Furthermore, another person, with tears streaming down his face, addressed the Buddha, saying:
"I am unable to examine for myself this world or the world beyond; doubt has arisen in my mind."

Now, appearing before the Buddha and contradicting the teachings of the scriptures of the Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, of the ten directions, we have been shrouded by the veils of the latent afflictions and failed to recognize our own transgressions.
We now all take refuge before the Buddha, confessing our sins without daring to conceal them; may the Buddha grant us his forgiveness.
"It is as if a foolish and ignorant person, having acted contrary to the principles of governance, beholds their own transgressions.
We pray that the Buddha, in his great compassion, will grant us forgiveness.
The Buddha addressed the fourfold assembly:
"Excellent, excellent!
Sons and daughters of good family who harbor doubts regarding this Dharma, yet observe their own transgressions and repent for those misfortunes, are like the sun dispelling the darkness."
At that time, Ānanda came forward and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"The members of this assembly now harbor doubts; will they also incur such offenses as these?"
The Buddha said,
"Ānanda! Although they harbored doubts, because they now repent their transgressions, the offenses of such persons shall remain light."
Ānanda asked again,
“I pray that the Buddha will explain this. The Buddha said:
"At the time of his approaching death, he will encounter the agonies of hell.
Within every single pore, he shall undergo countless and incalculable sufferings; yet even this is but the lingering breath of his remaining life."

Why is this? Because they have cast off the faults of doubt and regret in the presence of the Buddha, and have received the compassionate bestowal of grace and virtue from the countless Buddhas of the ten directions. Therefore, Ānanda!
Good sons and good daughters should examine yourselves: having obtained such a body as this, you shall encounter immeasurable suffering.
Upon hearing this sutra, you should rejoice and not harbor any doubt.

Those who do not wish to abandon the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Noble Sangha, nor the teachings of the Buddhas of the past, future, and present, should believe in this sutra and uphold, recite, chant, and read it.
Chapter 18: Entrustment The *Anavatapta-nirdeśa-sūtra*, Chapter Eighteen: Entrustment. The Venerable Ānanda addressed the World-Honored One, saying:
"Do all the Great Sages, the Buddhas, equally and identically preach the Wheel of Non-Retrogression?"
The Buddha said, “It is so;
they are equal and without distinction.
Ānanda asked the Buddha:
"If all Buddhas equally preach the wheel of non-retrogression, for what reason did the Great Sage just now say:

'If there are those who do not wish to distance themselves from the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha, or from the Buddhas of the past, future, and present whom the Buddha has manifested, they must not keep far from this scroll of the sutra'?"
Ānanda asked again: "What does the Buddha’s teaching illuminate and cause to flourish?"
The Buddha said:
“The assembly of those with the wheel of non-retrogression has gathered together to manifest the Buddha-dharma.
This seed of non-retrogression is that which the Tathāgata has expounded.”
Ānanda asked again:
"Are the bodhisattva mahāsattvas who have attained non-retrogression included among the assembly of noble ones?
The Buddha said:
“Ānanda! With pure and upright intention, they have resolved upon the mind of the Great Way.
Observe this intention: these individuals all belong to the assembly of those who are non-retrogressive.”
Ānanda said to the Buddha:
“It has never happened before.
The Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, employ skillful means according to the times to manifest and proclaim the Great Way.”
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, immediately scattered celestial flowers over the Buddha and uttered this verse of praise:
"May all people, relying upon skillful means (*upāya-kauśalya*), expound the scriptures."
The Buddha said, “Kauśika!

Those who hear this sutra and receive it with joy and faith—such people shall likewise use these skillful means to preach the Dharma and transform others, inspiring many to awakening; they shall be equal to me, without any difference.”
At that time, an immeasurable multitude of devas all made offerings to the World-Honored One with celestial flowers and spoke these words in unison:
"May all people attain this Dharma."
Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
"I only pray that the World-Honored One will establish great compassion, so that future generations may receive the benefits of this sūtra.
The Buddha told Ānanda:
“Good sons and good daughters who come to this assembly will certainly obtain this sutra volume in future lives.
Even if they should happen to fall into the great ocean, they shall obtain this sutra and will surely hear it.”
"Why is this? Because the spiritual transformations of all Buddhas of the past encompass the Dharma of this sutra.
Ānanda addressed the Buddha:
"This is due to the majestic spiritual power of the Buddhas of the past, and it is likewise established by the present Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas."
When these words were spoken, the trichiliocosm shook in six ways.

At that moment, before the Buddha, countless billions of hundreds of thousands of flowers and jewel lotuses spontaneously welled up from the earth, their universal radiance illuminating lands as numerous as the sands of the Ganges throughout the ten directions.

At that time, those in the assembly saw throughout the ten directions, in Buddha-worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, lotus flowers with hundreds of millions of billions of petals appearing before each World-Honored One; there was no one who did not perceive this.
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, transformed his own form into that of an elder. Holding various kinds of flowers, he distributed them among the fourfold assembly and spoke these words:
"I pray that you take these flowers and scatter them over the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, and further offer them as an act of worship for the profound meaning of this sutra."
The fourfold assembly followed these words, each taking flowers and scattering them over the various Buddhas.
The entire assembly saw that the scattered flowers, remaining above the various Buddhas, transformed into flower canopies.
At that time, the fourfold assembly each addressed the Buddha, saying:
"What is the fundamental omen for this?
How is it that the radiance is so exceedingly sublime?"

"The great earth shook, and furthermore, various precious flowers manifested by transformation appeared before the Buddha; the flowers that were scattered all transformed into jeweled canopies above every Buddha?
The Buddha said, "Ānanda!"
"All these are transformations and manifestations of the sūtra scrolls.
Therefore, you should know that this sūtra has been established and disseminated everywhere; those who receive it shall contemplate it.
At that time, Ānanda again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“Now, World-Honored One!
It is by virtue of Your holy intent that this sutra has been established.
The Buddha said:
"Establishing protection in this manner, even for the Buddhas of the present, it shall likewise be thus, equal and without distinction.
Ānanda asked the Buddha:
"What is the name of this sūtra scroll?"
"How should it be upheld? The Buddha said, "Ānanda!"

The name of this sutra is "Non-Reliance on Fruits and the Elimination of the Notion of Meritorious Traces. It is also called "The Śrāvakas, Pratyekabuddhas, and Those Who Have Attained the Path of Faith, the Way of Practice, the Once-Returner, the Non-Returner, and the Arhat. It is also called "The Conversion of Malignant Māras," and it is also called "The Adherence to the Six Pāramitās."
You should uphold it.
Why is this? If one hears this sutra and believes and delights in it, they shall immediately become fully endowed with the six perfections (ṣaṭ-pāramitā).
Ānanda asked again:
"How does one who believes with joy and upholds [this teaching] become complete in the six pāramitās?
The Buddha said to Ānanda:

"If sons or daughters of good family believe in and rejoice in this sutra without doubt, their practice of giving constitutes the perfection of giving; their non-violation and non-loss of the precepts constitute the perfection of morality; their patient endurance in all circumstances constitutes the perfection of patience; their freedom from indolence and abandonment of cowardice constitutes the perfection of vigor; their undertaking of activities with the same resolve as that of the Bodhisattva Never-Disparaging constitutes the perfection of meditation; and their state of total non-conceptuality and equanimity toward all phenomena constitutes the perfection of wisdom."
Therefore, Ānanda! This sūtra scroll is titled "The Six Perfections (Ṣaṭpāramitā)"; it is also called "The Vaipulya Dharma of the Non-retrogressive Wheel."
Ānanda addressed the Buddha:
“Indeed, World-Honored One!
To hear the name of this sutra brings such great benefit; how much more so for those who receive, uphold, recite, and chant it?”
The Buddha said, “It is so;
they are difficult to encounter. Ānanda asked again:
“How many kalpas can one transcend by hearing the name of this sutra?
The Buddha said, “Ānanda!
"Those who hear this Sūtra on the Wheel of Non-retrogression and believe it with joy shall transcend and eliminate the sufferings of countless hundreds of thousands of kalpas of birth and death.
Furthermore, as for those who, upon hearing it, cast aside arrogance and give rise to the aspiration for the Way—what of them?"
The Buddha said:
“Ānanda! The Buddhas have all bestowed upon them the prediction that they shall attain the resolve for the unsurpassed, right, and true path.”

At that time, before each member of the fourfold assembly, lotuses of immeasurable radiance and color appeared by transformation. Within each lotus were hundreds of thousands of countless other flowers. Each person, filled with joy, took a lotus to offer to the World-Honored One and, in unison, exclaimed:
"May we likewise encounter this Dharma in the world and, like you now, expound it through detailed analysis."
At that moment, the Buddha smiled, whereupon musical instruments resounded spontaneously and fragrances wafted throughout the ten directions.
Countless thousands of devas rained down flowers from the sky—sandalwood, fine gold, and celestial *manojñā* flowers—and the garments of the devas were scattered over the World-Honored One.
The venerable Ānanda knelt with his palms joined, stepped forward, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"The Buddha does not smile without cause; there must surely be a reason.
The Buddha said to Ānanda:

"Now, all those of the fourfold assembly—gods, nāgas, spirits, humans, and non-humans—who hear this sutra will, in their future births, invariably encounter this sutra as it is being expounded in its true meaning, no different from what occurs today under my guidance."
When the Buddha had spoken these words, the Venerable Ānanda, the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, and all the devas, humans, and worldlings were filled with joy.
Thus ends the lower fascicle of the *Anavatapta-nirdeśa-sūtra*.
